item.title: WNBA star Nneka Ogwumike has earned a little rest
item.description: Nneka Ogwumike's legacy was never in question winning a championship and league MVP within four years. Negotiating the largest collective bargaining agreement in pro sports for the WNBA ensures it.

item.title: To train robots, AI companies are paying people in India to film themselves doing chores
item.description: Men and women across India are being paid to record themselves doing domestic jobs as developers train AI robots to do household chores.

item.title: This week in science: sea monsters, long COVID patients' microbiome, elephant carcasses
item.description: NPR's science podcast Short Wave brings us stories about the hunting habits of ancient sea monsters, the microbiome of long COVID patients, and how elephant carcasses replenish the savannah.

item.title: The planned public execution has been canceled, but what message did it send?
item.description: President Trump announced that the Fort Hood attacker's execution will not be livestreamed. NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with New Yorker journalist Dexter Filkins, who witnessed a public execution.

item.title: Three years on, Israel still bars foreign journalists from entering Gaza
item.description: More than a year into a declared ceasefire in Gaza — and three years into the war — Israel still hasn't allowed foreign media independent access to Gaza.
